newsitem.title: UK: Charlton Athletic makes disappointing debut.
newsitem.headline: Charlton Athletic makes disappointing debut.

text.p: Shares in Charlton Athletic on Friday fell victim to the growing perception that football shares have become unrealistically valued. The first division club's shares opened at a 6 percent discount to their offer price.

Existing shareholders, season ticket holders and supporters had snapped up around 1.3 million shares priced at 76p. Charlton's institutional placing was also fully subscribed at 80p per share, valuing the club at 17.4 million stg.
But after opening on the Alternative Investment Market at 71p, the share price later slipped back to 56-1/2p, a discount of 26 percent.

"The fact that Charlton shares specifically opened at a discount is merely a reflection of the recent general concerns expressed about the sector rather than specific concerns about Charlton itself," said a company spokesman.
Investors have seen football stocks fall back from their peaks over the last few months amid worries over unrealistic premiums and growing supply.
In the last twelve months the number of quoted football clubs has jumped to 14 from just 5 a year ago.
"The market is definitely turning in the short term," the spokesman said. "But the fact that we have actually got the flotation away shows the underlying strength of Charlton's business."
The club is planning to use part of the 5.5 million stg net proceeds to boost capacity at the Valley stadium to 20,000.
Club chairman, Richard Murray subscribed for an additional 1.28 million shares, taking his interest in the club to 28 percent.

"I am very pleased with the success of the issue and delighted that we can now proceed with our ambitious plans for the further development of The Valley," Murray said. "Specifically the construction of the new main stand."
The south-east club is currently placed eighteenth out of 24 clubs in division one. The bottom three will be relegated to division two at the end of the season.
Investors have recently become more choosy about football shares, wary that the sector is increasingly crowded and much-hyped.

The success of cup and league winners Manchester United's flotation helped to encourage the rapid expansion of quoted football stocks. Shares in Manchester United remain among the strongest performing UK stocks. They rose almost 70 percent in the six months up to January.

But more recently the plight of Charlton's neighbour Millwall Holdings with its financial crisis and share suspension, together with analysts warnings that football shares had become overstretched, have dampened market enthusiasm.
